processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%, x = 15) ingots produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples using EDM for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process of this sample).
Solution-treated samples aged at 550 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching — the terminal step defining this sample.

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 550 °C for 1 h the 15Al alloy consists of an α (BCC) matrix with co-precipitated α-Mn and β-Mn; XRD of this condition shows α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn, indicating that the two Mn-rich phases coprecipitated before the α matrix fully transformed to β-Mn. Only a slight increase in hardness occurred over the solution-treated state, consistent with limited β-Mn formation at this low-temperature short-time aging.

unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 1 h the Vickers hardness increased only slightly over the solution-treated state (253.4 HV), reaching 380.2 ± 15.5 HV (b0037, Table 2).
The XRD pattern used for phase identification of the 15Al / 550 °C / 1 h condition is the black trace in Fig. 10, explicitly labelled '15Al 550 °C × 1 h' (figure_010, b0053).
The 15Al alloy attained an ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g at its peak-hardness condition (600 °C for 6 h, 965.6 HV), not at this 550 °C/1 h condition (b0008, b0077).
The optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness in the 15Al alloy was mainly 525–600 °C (b0038).

The β-Mn phase in the hardest 15Al sample has an intrinsic hardness of 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa (nanoindentation) and a measured composition of Mn 36.8 at.%, Al 14.3 at.%, Cu 2.8 at.% (b0060); these values pertain to the peak-aging sample, not the 550 °C/1 h sample.
